BLUETTI Apex 200 vs. Apex 300 for home backup

For home backup power, I'd lean toward the BLUETTI Apex 300, especially if you want to power refrigerators, lights, networking equipment, and potentially larger household appliances during an outage.

The Apex 200 is worth considering if your priority is a smaller, more affordable backup system for essential devices.

The important differences aren't just battery capacity. For home backup, you should compare AC output, 120V/240V support, expandability, and how each system connects to your home's electrical panel.

2. What matters most for home backup

240V support is the Apex 300's biggest advantage. It can support compatible 240V loads and more integrated home electrical configurations. The Apex 200 is primarily a 120V solution, even though its product specifications list a NEMA 14-50R outlet.

4. Expandability and long outages

Both models can use B300K and B500K expansion batteries. That means you don't have to choose the Apex 300 just to get more battery capacity.

The Apex 300 has an advantage for larger systems: a supported three-unit configuration can provide approximately 11.5kW of output, versus 6kW for the specified three-unit Apex 200 configuration. Both can approach 100kWh of storage with substantial expansion hardware. 
BLUETTI US

For a one- or two-day outage, I would prioritize buying enough battery capacity rather than paying extra solely for a few hundred watts of inverter output.

5. Price and value

One current Apex 300 listing:

Bluetti Apex 300 2764Wh/3840W Portable Power Station Dual Vo…

$1,374.99

FactoryPure

The Apex 200 is newly launched, and I couldn't verify a comparable live base-unit price. I'd compare actual delivered prices, including expansion batteries and transfer equipment.

My recommendation

Choose the Apex 300 if this is primarily a stationary home backup system, especially if you might add 240V circuits later. Choose the Apex 200 if you only need 120V essentials and it offers meaningful savings.

One question would make the recommendation much more specific:

Just essentials — refrigerator, internet, lights
Several home circuits through a transfer switch
Whole-home backup, including AC or 240V appliances
